{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Payer and budget: A sells to B2B SaaS teams paying from a product/growth software budget. B sells to individuals paying out of pocket. Business budgets usually make a first paid conversion inside 90 days easier.",
    "Price point: A's willingness to pay is documented at $25-$79/mo through several sourced pricing pages (Canny, Frill, Featul, Userback). A third-party study of 62 tools puts the median entry plan at $31.50/mo. B's $10-15/mo hypothesis rests on one anchor (Roam), against a free incumbent (Obsidian).",
    "Demand evidence: A's buyer complaint ('$50-80/month on a feedback widget is ridiculous for a side project') is sourced. It points to a concrete wedge, a lower-priced or simpler tier for early-stage products. B's demand quotes describe a general pain (scattered links, unstructured research) but say nothing about paying for a new tool.",
    "Warning signals: B's own brief records that a funded team (WorldBrain) has pursued this exact pitch since 2018 without mainstream traction. It also notes Tana repositioned away from pure PKM, and that firsthand accounts say retrieval and habit, not connecting more sources, drive churn. Each of these weakens B's core premise.",
    "Feasibility: A's workflow is simple and well documented, and the brief cites solo builders already shipping it with AI-agent integrations. That supports a six-week build and launch by one operator. B adds extra friction for a solo launch: indexing browsing history and personal documents raises privacy concerns.",
    "Caveat: A's case against is serious. The category is crowded and commoditized, with 73 tools tracked, free tiers standard, and incumbents already shipping AI features. A wins as the better first bet, not as a strong one."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B claims WorldBrain's Memex 'proved there is at least enough enthusiast demand to attract funding,' but the only citation is a GitHub repository, which shows neither funding nor paying demand. B's demand evidence is also thin: a 2020 HN comment and one researcher blog post, neither showing willingness to pay. Its scale claim for Obsidian (~1M users) is an 'estimated' figure from Wikipedia and concerns a free product, so it does not show demand for a paid new entrant.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both ideas sit in saturated categories, and both briefs list unresolved open questions. A wins mainly because its payer has a budget, its price points and willingness to pay are better sourced, and B's brief contains several documented signals that monetizing personal knowledge tools at a solo price point is hard. A's acquisition-cost picture is weak: the cited Google Ads benchmark ($5.42 average CPC) is generic, not specific to this category, and the Product Hunt evidence comes from a single Reddit post. The 90-day outcome for A therefore depends heavily on finding an unclaimed wedge, which the brief does not establish."
}
